visuals.title: Where it hits
visuals.text: Nerve roots leaving the spine, felt along the nerve in the arm or leg.

visuals.title: Cauda equina red flags
visuals.text: Back pain plus urinary retention is cauda equina until proven otherwise.

visuals.title: When to image
nodes: No imaging initially; X-ray of little use
MRI spine if red flags or not settling

events.x: Not settling: routine spinal surgery referral
Cauda equina or acute deficit: urgent referral

visuals.title: Why the deficit localises
nodes: Its dermatome, myotome and reflex affected

glossary.Spinal nerve root: The part of a spinal nerve as it leaves the spinal cord and exits between vertebrae.
glossary.Dermatomal: Following the strip of skin supplied by one spinal nerve root.
glossary.Myotomal: Affecting the group of muscles supplied by one spinal nerve root.
glossary.Degenerative spine disease: Age-related wear of the discs and joints of the spine.
glossary.Cervical: Relating to the neck part of the spine, C1 to C7.
glossary.Lumbar: Relating to the lower back part of the spine, L1 to L5.
glossary.Radiating: Spreading out from one place along the path of a nerve.
glossary.Medial scapular border: The inner edge of the shoulder blade, nearest the spine.
glossary.Deltoid: The large shoulder muscle that lifts the arm out to the side.
glossary.Supraspinatus: Rotator cuff muscle that starts lifting the arm away from the body.
glossary.Infraspinatus: Rotator cuff muscle that turns the arm outwards.
glossary.Biceps reflex: Elbow flexion when the biceps tendon is tapped, testing C5 and C6.
glossary.Wrist flexors: Forearm muscles that bend the wrist forwards.
glossary.Ulnar: On the little finger side of the forearm or hand.
glossary.Hip flexion: Lifting the thigh forwards at the hip.
glossary.Hip adduction: Bringing the leg in towards the midline.
glossary.Hip abduction: Moving the leg out to the side.
glossary.Knee extension: Straightening the knee, done by the quadriceps.
glossary.Malleolus: The bony bump on either side of the ankle.
glossary.Dorsum of foot: The top surface of the foot.
glossary.Plantar flexion: Pointing the foot downwards, as when standing on tiptoe.
glossary.Surgical emergency: A condition needing an operation within hours to prevent permanent harm.
glossary.Reduced tone: Floppy muscles that offer less resistance than normal to passive movement.
glossary.Anal sphincter tone: The tightness of the muscle ring around the anus, checked on rectal examination.
glossary.MRI spine: A magnetic scan showing discs, nerve roots and the spinal cord in detail.
glossary.Conservative management: Treatment without surgery, such as painkillers, physio and time.
glossary.Physiotherapy: Exercise and movement-based treatment to restore function and reduce pain.
glossary.Steroid injection: Corticosteroid injected near the nerve root to reduce inflammation.
glossary.Neurological deficit: Loss of normal nerve function, such as weakness, numbness or lost reflexes.
glossary.Inflammatory mediators: Chemicals released by damaged tissue that cause inflammation and irritate nerves.
glossary.Spinal canal: The tunnel through the vertebrae that contains the spinal cord and nerve roots.
glossary.Reflex arc: The nerve loop from a sensory receptor to the spinal cord and back to a muscle.
glossary.Disc space: The gap between two vertebrae occupied by an intervertebral disc.
glossary.Lumbosacral roots: The nerve roots from the lower spine and sacrum that supply the legs, bladder and bowel.
glossary.Spinal cord terminus: The lower end of the spinal cord, around L1/L2 in adults.
glossary.Paracetamol: A simple painkiller and fever reducer, first choice for mild pain.
glossary.Postero-lateral: Towards the back and side; the usual direction a disc bulges, hitting the nerve root.
